pa_o_chain_reaction_buttress.blurb: A buttress in the High Rocks gorge above Tohickon Creek, in Ralph Stover State Park, Bucks County. It holds eleven routes, most of them traditionally protected, with one sport line and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.4 and climb into the 5.10 range, so it suits a mixed party, though the harder lines are real tests. The rock is argillite. The wall catches sun for most of the day, which makes it pleasant on cold days. Many routes now finish at bolts with chains, and the buttress gets busy on weekends, sometimes with newer climbers on the ropes. Expect a steep descent gully and a walk along the cliff base to reach it.

pa_eversince_area.blurb: A small cluster of roughly eight boulders spread over a steep wooded hillside in Rothrock State Forest, a short drive from State College in Central Pennsylvania. There are eleven problems, all bouldering, mostly easy to moderate in the V1 and V2 range with a few at V3 and one at V4. That makes it a good place for newer boulderers or a quick session rather than a project venue. The walk in is short, about five to ten minutes depending on which of two trails you take, and the ground is steep, so watch your footing when moving between boulders.

pa_of_mice_and_men_area.blurb: A bouldering zone in the northwest corner of the Hangar 18 section of Haycock Mountain, near Nockamixon in Bucks County. It holds eleven problems with a wide spread: a couple of easy ones at V1 and V2, a solid middle of V4 and V5 problems, and a few hard lines up to V8. Hangar 18 has the shortest walk-in of any Haycock area, so this is a convenient stop for a session rather than a long day. Bring several pads, since some of the taller problems finish well off the ground.

pa_xmann_s_run.blurb: A cliff section at Safe Harbor on the Susquehanna River in south-central Pennsylvania, roughly 25 minutes from Lancaster, just south of Mann's Run. It has eleven climbs, mostly bolted sport lines plus a couple of trad routes and a single boulder problem. Grades sit mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a few at 5.11 and one easier line, so it works for solid intermediate climbers. The cliff has a lower part beside the trail and an upper tier above it, reached by climbing one of the routes. You get here by walking or biking in along the river trail.
